content_html:
How Neurons, Dendrites, Axons & Synapses Relate

Dendrites receive inputs at synapses → the soma integrates them → if threshold is crossed at the axon hillock, an action potential travels down the axon (often myelinated) → at the axon terminal it triggers neurotransmitter release at a synapse onto the next neuron’s dendrite. The cycle continues through neural circuits.

  • Dendrites receive graded synaptic inputs (EPSPs/IPSPs) on spines.
  • The soma integrates inputs; the axon hillock initiates all‑or‑none action potentials when threshold is exceeded.
  • The axon conducts action potentials; myelin increases speed via saltatory conduction at nodes of Ranvier.
  • Axon terminals convert electrical spikes into chemical signals at synapses, releasing neurotransmitter into the cleft to bind postsynaptic receptors on dendritic spines.
